preserved_primary_reviews.rationale: There is no boundary evidence of any class at 40:9. The verse opens ולקחת את שמן המשחה ומשחת את המשכן - a plain weqatal 2ms, indistinguishable in form from 40:8 ושמת את החצר סביב ונתת את מסך שער החצר, and from 40:10, 40:11, 40:12 - so the entire speech 40:1-15 is one unbroken weqatal chain under a single messenger formula. MT confirms: there is no pe or setumah anywhere between the petuchah at 39:43 and the setumah at 40:16, so 40:1-16 is one Masoretic paragraph. The topic shift the decision cites (arrangement vs consecration) is real but is class-5 marker-free content observation; and if a topic split were taken, 40:12 והקרבת את אהרן ואת בניו אל פתח אהל מועד is at least as marked, since it is where the object-list gives way to persons. The decision's own rejected alternative (merge with 141) is the better-evidenced reading.

preserved_primary_reviews.rationale: FORM: 'consecration_instruction_speech' is well distinguished by content from 'erection_instruction_speech' -- arrangement/placement vs. sanctification are genuinely different procedural categories (setting furniture in place, then anointing it). SEAM: opens on 'You shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle' (v.9), a fresh imperative clause, but -- as the decision's own rejected alternative candidly notes -- no new messenger formula separates this from 141; both are part of the same uninterrupted speech begun at 40:1. The split therefore rests on content/procedural-sequence grounds alone, the same kind of evidence used (more cautiously) for 116/117 and 119. It holds up reasonably well given the clear procedural pivot (place things, then sanctify them) and the parallel closing formula each half receives (v.8's screen notice; v.15's everlasting-priesthood promise). LARGER UNIT: worth noting that ch.40's execution narrative (143) never explicitly re-narrates the anointing of Aaron and his sons in the same detail given here -- it is covered only by the blanket compliance statement at v.16 -- a genuine compositional asymmetry between instruction and execution at the very end of the book, though outside the scope of what can be resolved from Exodus alone. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: the no-formula continuation is real and duly flagged; the content pivot is sufficient but this is a softer seam than the fully formula-marked boundaries elsewhere in this cluster.

This is a genuine, unresolved consistency defect rather than a documentation nicety.
